query: What learner needs and pain points appear in survey responses?

per_column.name: primary_challenge_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorises the subject/domain where difficulty appears, giving a strong grouping axis for pain points. Samples align well (mathematics for algebra, literacy for reading, participation_discussion for the discussion-averse class). 'not_present' correctly used for positive/domain-silent responses.

per_column.name: engagement_and_motivation_signal
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to learner needs; provides a graded motivation axis rather than a bare sentiment flag. Readings are mostly sound (high_intrinsic for the pause-and-note student, disengagement for cameras-off class). ED-0001 labelled disengagement is defensible though the response reads more as frustration than disengagement.

per_column.name: social_interaction_need
per_column.rationale: A genuine new axis on peer/collaboration needs relevant to the query. Mostly grounded, but ED-0001 ('miss being able to raise my hand quietly') mapped to peer_collaboration_missed is a stretch—that phrase is about teacher interaction, not peers. ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' → peer_collaboration_missed is well grounded.

per_column.name: hands_on_material_dependency
per_column.rationale: Useful axis for lab/materials pain points. However some values appear invented: ED-0001 (algebra, camera freeze) labelled hands_on_critical_for_learning has no material basis in the text, and ED-0003 (reading logout issues) labelled manipulatives_or_equipment_essential is unsupported. This inflates a category the source does not warrant.

per_column.name: instructional_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Captures teacher-responsiveness pain points central to the query. Readings are reasonable (slow_response for the frozen/lost-teacher cases, asynchronous_but_adequate for the pause-lecture student). Distribution is not near-constant and gives modelling leverage.

per_column.name: modality_alignment_with_learner
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes sync/async/video needs, a meaningful axis for remote-learning pain points. Samples align well (video_replay for pause-and-note student, live_synchronous_essential for real-time-dependent cases). 'not_present' appropriately used.

per_column.name: identity_and_confidence_impact
per_column.rationale: Emotional/confidence dimension is directly relevant to learner needs and not a mere sentiment restatement (it is directional and specific). Grounded readings: anxiety for the crying second grader, confidence_gained for the self-paced student.

judge.rationale: The added columns form a coherent, non-redundant set of categorical axes (domain, engagement, social need, materials, instruction, modality, confidence) that give real grouping and comparison leverage for identifying learner needs and pain points—none are trivial constants or bare sentiment flags. Groundedness is generally strong, with sensible 'not_present' handling for silent rows. The main weakness is hands_on_material_dependency, where several values (e.g., materials/manipulatives assigned to camera-freeze algebra and logout-plagued reading responses) assert dependencies the source text does not support, and a couple of social_interaction_need mappings over-read teacher-interaction cues as peer needs. Overall useful with localized hallucination risk in one column.
